title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
notes: An architecture comparison with an official repository. The parameter-efficiency claim is the interesting one: it compares two architectures at matched parameter counts, which is exactly the kind of controlled comparison that shrinks well.

claims.text: A DenseNet reaches lower test error than a ResNet with a comparable number of parameters on CIFAR-10.
claims.notes: Both arms are convnets on CIFAR-10 at matched capacity; shrinks to small variants cleanly.

claims.text: DenseNets need fewer parameters than ResNets to reach the same accuracy.
claims.notes: The parameter-efficiency claim, measurable by matching accuracy and comparing sizes at small scale.

claims.text: The advantage of DenseNet over ResNet is larger on CIFAR-100 and without data augmentation.
claims.notes: A comparison of two effect sizes, which needs more statistical power than three seeds give.

claims.text: Dense connectivity acts as a regulariser, reducing overfitting on tasks without data augmentation.
claims.notes: Plausible at small scale but entangled with the architecture change itself.

claims.text: DenseNet-BC with 190 layers reaches 3.46% error on CIFAR-10 with data augmentation.
claims.notes: A headline number from a 190-layer network.

claims.text: DenseNets achieve comparable accuracy to ResNets on ImageNet with half the parameters and half the computation.
claims.notes: ImageNet-scale training, far outside a small CPU budget.

claims.text: The compression and bottleneck layers (DenseNet-BC) improve parameter efficiency over the plain DenseNet.
claims.notes: An internal ablation of the same architecture, which is the cleanest kind of claim here.
